title: Man. Post. Cap. IV: PLAC — Vir Doctus dat manus; originalis = condition
pass_a_gloss: PLAC. By this reply the learned man openly contradicts himself, and while he seems to reply, he does not reply nevertheless, but gives his hands. For the matter was about original justice, as is clear from my argument. Which then of those two justices which he distinguished is original justice? Is it that supernatural one, of the homeland, of glorified man? Certainly not. For Adam was not endowed with that before he sinned: he was not going to propagate that into posterity. Is it therefore the natural justice, of the way, of created man, the original justice about which the argument was concerned? But the learned man confesses that this Justice was the condition of the promise. He confesses therefore that it was not promised: which is what I had set out to prove, and he himself had denied. But if it was not promised, its privation was not the death denounced by the threat. Which is what it was incumbent on me to prove.
pass_b_english: PLAC. This answer openly contradicts the learned man himself. He seems to reply, yet does not—he yields. We were arguing about original justice, as my case shows. Of the two justices he split apart, which is original? The supernatural homeland justice of glorified man? No. Adam lacked that before the fall and was never going to hand it down.

So original justice in the argument is natural justice—of the way, of created man. But Garissoles admits that justice was the condition of the promise. He therefore admits it was not promised—the very point I meant to prove, which he had denied. If it was not promised, losing it was not the death the threat denounced. That is what I had to establish.
source_text: PLAC. Hac responsione sibi Vir Doctus aperte contradicit, & cum videatur respondere, non respondet tamen, sed dat manus. Agebatur enim de justitia originali, ut patet ex meo argumento. Utra igitur duarum illarum, quas distinxit, justitiarum est justitia originalis? Num illa supernaturalis, patriae, hominis glorificati? Non certe. Non enim illa Adamus priusquam peccaret praeditus erat: non illam erat propagaturus in posteros. Est igitur justitia naturalis, viae, hominis creati, justitia originalis de qua agebatur in argumento? Atqui Vir doctus confitetur hanc Justitiam fuisse conditionem promissionis. Confitetur ergo non fuisse promissam: id quod probare institueram, & ipse negaverat. Quod si non fuit promissa, eius privatio non fuit mors comminatione denunciata. Id quod mihi probandum incumbebat.
